categories.main_business_segments: Okura Industrial Co., Ltd. operates three main business segments: Synthetic Resins (manufacturing and sales of polyethylene and polypropylene films and related products), Advanced Materials (production and sales of optical functional films and related high-performance materials), and Building Materials (manufacturing and sales of particle boards, processed boards, and wood-based construction materials). The company also engages in real estate development, housing construction, hotel operations, and information systems as ancillary businesses.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include extrusion and stretching processes for plastic films, fine coating, and various secondary processing techniques. It leverages advanced film manufacturing for both packaging and high-performance optical applications, as well as wood processing and composite material technologies for building materials. R&D focuses on material science, recycling technologies, and the development of functional films for electronics, energy, and life sciences.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include manufacturers in the food packaging, electronics (especially display and optical device makers), construction and housing industries, and local governments (for eco-friendly products). The company also serves the hospitality sector through its hotel business and provides IT solutions to pharmacies and other businesses.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are primarily based in Japan, with major production facilities in Kagawa, Shiga, Saitama, Kumamoto, and Okayama. The company also has subsidiaries and affiliates in China and Vietnam, and a small portion of its business is international, but over 90% of sales and assets are domestic.
categories.supply_chain_position: Okura Industrial operates mainly in the midstream and downstream segments of the supply chain, processing raw materials (such as petrochemicals and wood) into films, boards, and functional materials, and delivering finished or semi-finished products to manufacturers, builders, and end-users.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding business domains, enhancing capital efficiency, and strengthening shareholder returns. R&D is focused on sustainability (decarbonization, resource circulation), digital transformation (DX), and innovation in high-value-added materials for electronics, energy, life sciences, and mobility. The company emphasizes ESG/SDGs, aiming to increase the share of environmentally beneficial products and reduce CO2 emissions.
categories.revenue_model: The company primarily generates revenue through the sale of manufactured products (films, boards, materials), contract processing, and construction projects. Ancillary revenue streams include hotel operations, real estate leasing, and IT system development. Revenue is recognized upon delivery or completion of contractual obligations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese and Asian manufacturers of synthetic resins, packaging films, optical films, and building materials. The company is a mid-sized player with a strong domestic presence and niche strengths in high-performance films and eco-friendly materials. It maintains close relationships with large clients such as Sumitomo Chemical and leverages long-term partnerships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending December 2024, consolidated net sales were 81.2 billion yen, with operating profit of 4.56 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 4.36 billion yen. The company has a stable financial base (equity ratio ~60%), moderate growth (3% sales increase YoY), and a workforce of about 1,900 employees. Growth is steady but faces challenges from market fluctuations and raw material costs.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Okura Industrial differentiates itself through advanced material processing technologies, a strong focus on sustainability (eco-friendly and recycled products), and the ability to provide customized solutions for diverse industries. Its unique value lies in combining material innovation with environmental responsibility, offering high-quality, functional films and boards that support both customer needs and societal challenges.
